drug_class: Combination antidiabetic medication (SGLT2 inhibitor + DPP-4 inhibitor + Biguanide)
purpose: This medication is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines three different medicines that work in different ways to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range. It is used along with diet and exercise to manage your diabetes.
how_it_works: Metformin helps your liver from making too much sugar and helps your body use insulin better. Linagliptin helps your body release more insulin after meals and lowers the amount of sugar your liver puts out. Empagliflozin works through your kidneys to remove extra sugar from your blood by passing it out in your urine, so your body gets rid of it naturally.
common_side_effects: You may notice nausea, stomach upset, diarrhea, or a decreased appetite especially when starting the medication — taking it with food helps a lot. You may also have more urinary tract or yeast infections than usual because of the extra sugar passing through your urine. Some people notice more frequent urination.
warnings: Call your doctor right away if you have signs of a serious but rare condition called lactic acidosis — symptoms include muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, feeling cold, or feeling dizzy. Do not take this medicine if your kidneys are not working well. Stop taking it before any surgery or procedure using contrast dye and tell your doctor you take it. Watch for signs of a rare but serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene — pain, redness, or swelling in the genital or rectal area needs immediate medical attention. It can also cause low blood pressure, so stay well hydrated.
typical_dosing: This medicine is usually taken once a day with the morning meal. Your doctor will decide the right strength for you based on your current diabetes medicines and kidney function. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, cut, or chew it. Always follow exactly what your doctor prescribes.
